extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors, journal editors, and stakeholders interested in journal-independent peer review (particularly in biomedical sciences)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and metrics for Review Commons, a journal-independent peer review platform that produces refereed preprints and forwards reviews to partner journals; the page summarizes goals, survey results, operational metrics, and implementation lessons from the first 9 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus peer review on the science
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons explicitly asks reviewers to focus on evaluating and improving the science for its own sake, without a journal in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid asking reviewers to act as gatekeepers who evaluate fit relative to a journal’s editorial standards; reviews should be collegial, reasonable, and unbiased, aimed at improving the manuscript rather than assessing journal fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase efficiency by eliminating cycles of re-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner journals agree to consider papers without repeating peer review, with the goal of reducing duplicate rounds of peer review that occur when papers move between journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model targets the estimated large amount of reviewer time lost to re-reviewing (cited as ~15 million hours per year across fields) by forwarding refereed preprint reviews to affiliate journals to avoid new review cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerate transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable and encourage authors to post a refereed preprint including review reports and their rebuttal so peer review is disclosed earlier and is visible to readers prior to journal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refereed preprints are visible on bioRxiv under a peer review tab and the reviews are available in a machine-readable form via the hypothes.is API. Affiliates have implemented transparent review; authors may elect early disclosure to 'support open science.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability/portability of referee reports across journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee reports must be usable by a broad variety of journals so forwarded reviews can inform editorial decisions at multiple affiliate journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major implementation challenge is obtaining reports that are broadly portable; evidence of portability is that 16 journals in the consortium have accepted papers based on reports forwarded by Review Commons, indicating utility across journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness: time to return peer reviews to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of how quickly Review Commons returns peer reviews to authors whose manuscripts were sent for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over the evaluation period the median time to return peer reviews was 37 days; this is a key operational metric for assessing the service’s speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author revision time after receiving reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: How long authors take to revise manuscripts and respond to reviewer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors spent a median of 27 days revising and responding, which affects overall time-to-publication and uptake of posting refereed preprints (authors often cite need for more time to revise as a reason not to post).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate journal decision times after transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: How quickly affiliate journals return a first decision and accept manuscripts after receiving forwarded reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliate journals returned a first decision in a median of 8 days and accepted manuscripts, on average, 11 days after that (this average includes papers accepted at first decision). Manuscripts are transferred to a median of two affiliate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of duplicate peer review (affiliate behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether affiliate journals seek additional peer review after receiving Review Commons reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliates did not seek additional peer review in 98% of papers they rejected and in 86% of papers they accepted, indicating the system’s effectiveness at avoiding duplicate peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency outcome: proportion of published papers with transparent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraction of papers published after Review Commons review that are accompanied by transparent peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 90% of papers published after Review Commons review are accompanied by transparent peer review, showing that Review Commons disclosure is being maintained through to publication in most cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uptake of posting refereed preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of manuscripts that received reviews from Review Commons and were posted as refereed preprints, and authors' reasons for (not) posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 30% of manuscripts that received reviews were posted as refereed preprints during the evaluation period. All authors who posted cited support for open science; the most popular reason for not posting was needing more time to revise. Many respondents (about 1/3 to 1/2) answered 'don't know' to aspects of the survey about posting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author perceptions of review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: How authors perceive the nature of the reviews they received via Review Commons compared to traditional journal-based review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveyed corresponding authors reported that reviews were more collegial, reasonable, and unbiased than those received in traditional processes. However, many authors remained uncertain about the overall speed and efficiency of the publishing process, likely because many papers were still in process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention to increase refereed preprint posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational step to help authors understand benefits of posting refereed preprints after receiving reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASAPbio/Review Commons implemented an opportunity for authors to consult with the Managing Editor after receiving their reviews; anecdotal evidence suggests these discussions help authors appreciate potential benefits and may increase posting uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat about early/limited data
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on interpretation due to early-stage data and truncated distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the service is young, many manuscripts were still in process; the authors caution waiting for more manuscripts to go through the system before drawing firm conclusions about reductions in time to publication or other outcomes.
